articles.title: Matias Fernandez-Pardo transfer news: Newcastle sign Lille forward ahead of transfer deadline in deal worth £51m
articles.summary: Matias Fernandez-Pardo scored eight goals in 29 Ligue 1 games last season for Lille; he has been capped five times by Belgium and was part of their World Cup squad this summer; Newcastle pay Lille £51m for the 21-year-old
articles.body:
Fernandez-Pardo has penned a long-term contract and will wear the No 20 shirt at St James' Park. The deal brings Newcastle's summer spending to £262m.

Newcastle see the signing of forward Fernandez-Pardo as on a par with that of Nico Gonzalez, who joined the club last week from Man City for £50m.

He scored eight goals in 41 appearances for Lille last season and was named in Belgium's squad for the 2026 World Cup. His call-up came after he had initially switched his international allegiance to Spain, where he featured in youth-team training camps but never made a competitive appearance.

His arrival will allow Nick Woltemade to leave on loan, with Juventus in direct talks with Newcastle over the German striker.

Speaking to the club's official channels, Fernandez-Pardo said: "I spoke to the head coach and he really showed how much he wanted me to be here. In terms of my own career progression, it made complete sense to come, so I didn't hesitate at all. "I know the club, I know about the stadium, I know it's a fantastic atmosphere. I've followed the team. What I've seen is a very ambitious team, wants to attack, get forward, really chase teams and go after them, and that's really something I want to take part in as well."

Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle added: "Matias is a highly technical player with explosiveness in his game. He can score and assist, he has courage, and he has the ability to take players on. We're sure our supporters will enjoy watching him play."

European football expert Julien Laurens on Sky Sports News:

I think it's a really smart signing by Newcastle. To have replaced Woltemade with someone like him who fits the Jaissle system.

"That verticality, that running and the pace. Fernandez-Pardo will be perfect for that. He's a winger at heart but with all the skills that are required, he moved into a No 9 because of the smart runs that he can make and that he presses so well.

"He's just relentless in what he does on the pitch and that's perfect. If he and Yoane Wissa can partner well together with Will Osula, who's a slightly different profile, certainly in terms of height and physicality. Then I think you've got a great core there for Jaissle.

'I expected Woltemade to stay and fight for his spot at Newcastle'

"I expected Nick Woltemade to stay to fight because I expected him to gain more match practice under the new coach. It's a German connection, but aside from that, he wanted to stay and fight.

"But we have to talk about the fact that Newcastle increased the pressure with a new signing from France for €60m (£51m), so there was no space for Nick Woltemade. Let's see what will happen in Italy.

"It's a loan move. As I understand it, it's also without an option or obligation to buy.

"The package is around €4m (£3.4m). Let's see. I'm not a big fan of these big loan moves before the deadline. I have seen that with Randal Kolo Muani. Fingers crossed, because we need a very strong Nick Woltemade for the national team."

Newcastle turn down Forest bids for Murphy

Meanwhile, Newcastle have turned down multiple Deadline Day offers from Nottingham Forest for Jacob Murphy , with the latest being £15m.

Newcastle have told the winger he has a future at the club and new boss Matthias Jaissle sees him as key experience in the dressing room.

Forest had an opening offer of £10m rejected by Newcastle last week.

articles.title: ‘No one else like him’: Argentinians rally for Lionel Messi
articles.summary: Residents of Buenos Aires say they will miss the football legend who won the 2022 World Cup for Argentina.
articles.body:
Buenos Aires, Argentina – In the La Boca neighbourhood, home to the Boca Juniors stadium and a place which lives and breathes football, people are taking turns to be photographed in front of huge murals depicting football legend Lionel Messi holding the 2022 World Cup.

Across the city, monuments have been illuminated in Argentina’s blue and white in honour of the national hero, who has announced his retirement from international football after two decades during which he was transformed from young prodigy to national icon.

On Monday, football clubs around the country were singing songs for Messi and mounting banners showing him holding the World Cup he helped to win for his country. The Argentine Football Association is planning a farewell match to thank him for his extraordinary service.

Messi announced his departure from the national team this week on social media with a handwritten letter that he says he wrote two days after losing the World Cup final against Spain this year. He said he had “nothing else to give”.

“It was a decision that hurt – and still hurts deep down – but I understand that the time has come,” he wrote on Instagram on Monday.

While the news has not come as a total surprise – Messi is 39 years old and has recently lost his father, Jorge Messi, who played a crucial role in his career – fans are nevertheless devastated.

“We are going to continue loving Messi, not just for football but for his humility, for who he is; that’s the most important thing about Messi,” fan Sebastian Luna tells Al Jazeera. “It’s football; it’s over, but Messi will always be in our hearts”.

Some are calling for his number 10 jersey to be retired along with him. Alas, the International Federation of Association Football (FIFA) rules won’t allow it – the team has already tried.

Messi played six World Cups for Argentina, and for years, he struggled with constant criticism for failing to win one.

The ⁠former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain forward, who now plays ⁠for Inter Miami, has been repeatedly compared unfavourably with the football legend Diego Maradona – who also helped Argentina win one World Cup in 1986. But that all changed when Argentina won in Qatar, propelling Messi to the status of national symbol for all Argentinians across political and social divides. Now, they have two heroes to celebrate.

“I saw Maradona; I saw many players – Kempes – but Messi is superlative,” says fan Carlos Sciata in Buenos Aires. His retirement is “like a bucket of cold water, but well, it was something that could happen, especially after his father’s death. But we are going to miss him a lot. There is no one else like him,” he adds.

The record eight-time Ballon d’Or winner became his country’s record appearance maker and scorer, with 125 goals in 207 games, ⁠having transformed a complicated relationship with the national team into a story of redemption and triumph.

Tributes have poured in since his announcement on Monday.

Angel Di Maria, who played alongside Messi in their FIFA 2022 World Cup triumph in Qatar , said it was “so hard” to know fans will not be able to see the talismanic forward in the sky blue and white colours of Argentina any more.

“I only know that I was born in the right century to be able to see you, enjoy you, and on top of that, to share all these years with you on the national team,” Di Maria declared.

Rodrigo De Paul, Messi’s Argentinian teammate at his Major League Soccer club Inter Miami, applauded the record eight-time Ballon d’Or winner’s “unconditional love” for the country.

“Just thank you, the greatest of all time, thank you for making us so, so happy, you can’t imagine how many smiles you brought!!” he added.

Despite hoping for a final triumph at the World Cup this year, Argentina lost 1-0 to Spain in the final.

Now, Argentina is preparing for what comes next.

Messi’s departure leaves an enormous void for football fans, and questions are being raised about the future of coach Lionel Scaloni and the team he built around the star player.

Off the pitch, Argentinian football is facing problems of its own, with the Argentine Football Association (AFA) under investigation amid serious allegations of corruption and financial irregularities.

But for today, it is all about saying goodbye at the end of an era. Messi represents a collective source of happiness in a country that has endured economic and political upheaval.

The one man who makes all Argentinians proud summed it up in his farewell message on Monday: “I leave with the ‌peace ‌of mind and pride of having given you – alongside my teammates – moments we once only dreamed of,” he wrote.

articles.title: Malick Fofana transfer news: Lyon winger at centre of Premier League tug-of-war as Crystal Palace and Sunderland agree deals
articles.summary: Malick Fofana looked set to join Sunderland after the club made significant progress in their pursuit of the 20-year-old, who had also attracted interest from Arsenal; Palace moved to swoop in on Sunderland's deal; Black Cats have been given hope that their deal is still alive
articles.body:
Fofana had looked set to join Sunderland after the Black Cats made significant progress in their pursuit of the 20-year-old, who had also attracted interest from Arsenal.

Sky Sports News understands Fofana was at Lyon airport on Tuesday afternoon with two private jets waiting for him to make his decision - one bound for London and the other for Sunderland.

The extraordinary situation has developed after Palace moved to swoop in on Sunderland's deal for the 20-year-old, who had been expected to join the Black Cats after they agreed terms with Lyon earlier on Tuesday.

Sunderland's agreement is worth up to £30m, comprising a £25.7m fixed fee plus £4.3m in add-ons.

Fofana had been given permission to travel for a medical after Sunderland reached their agreement with Lyon and had a five-year contract ready for him.

However, Sky Sports News also revealed Palace had entered direct communication with the player in an attempt to convince him to move to Selhurst Park.

Palace have now secured their own club-to-club agreement with Lyon and are working on the formalities of the transfer. However, the Black Cats have been given hope that their deal to sign the winger is still alive.

Sky Sports News understands Sunderland are putting plans in place to give the player a medical in France.

Sunderland are also pressing ahead with an alternative deal should their move for Fofana ultimately fall through.

They are in talks with Benfica for Dodi Lukebakio , although their preference remains to discover whether Fofana will choose Sunderland or Palace.

Sunderland had been exploring moves for Jack Grealish and Igor Paixao as they looked to strengthen their attack before Tuesday's transfer deadline.

They had made an offer for Brazilian winger Paixao, which was rejected by Marseille, with negotiations proving difficult.

There was also a belief that Grealish would prefer to remain in the north west, with the Manchester City player in talks with Everton. That led Sunderland to consider Fofana as a viable alternative.

On Monday, Fofana remained an option for Sunderland going into Deadline Day amid the belief that Paixao would stay at Marseille.

The situation then moved quickly on Tuesday morning with Sunderland agreeing a deal with Lyon for Fofana, and the winger given permission to travel for a medical and a five-year contract expected to follow.

Arsenal had also been interested in the Belgian winger.

But Fofana had not completed his medical with Sunderland, contrary to reports, leaving the door open for Palace to make their move.

Palace's intervention has now turned what appeared to be a straightforward Sunderland transfer into one of the most intriguing deals of Deadline Day.

articles.title: Harvey Elliott to Valencia: Liverpool midfielder joins on season-long loan
articles.summary: Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott joins Valencia on a season-long loan
articles.body:
Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott has joined Valencia on a loan deal until the end of the season.

BBC Sport understands there is no option or obligation for the La Liga side to sign the 23-year-old permanently at the end of the campaign.

The midfielder arrived in Spain on Monday night to complete the move after Liverpool and Valencia reached an agreement over a deal earlier in the day.

It is the second consecutive season Elliott has been loaned out by Liverpool , having spent last season at Aston Villa .

After featuring regularly for the Reds during pre-season, Elliott was left out of the squads to face Newcastle and Nottingham Forest by new head coach Andoni Iraola.

The former England Under-21 international's contract with Liverpool runs until 2028.

Elliott joined Liverpool from Fulham aged 16 in 2019 and spent the 2020-21 season on loan at Blackburn Rovers in the Championship.

Valencia failed to qualify for Europe last season after finishing ninth in La Liga. They are currently 16th in the table after failing to win any of their first three matches.

articles.title: College athletics is eating itself, and LSU is at the head of the table
articles.summary: LSU's battle with the SEC is a microcosm of the unraveling of college athletics.
articles.body:
You ever read a college sports headline in the year 2026, step back for a second, and think, How did we get here?

How did we get to the point that players on actual NFL rosters are rejoining the college ranks?

How did we get to the point that serious discussions are being had about a 24-team football playoff that absolutely nobody wants?

How did we get to the point that Congress — freaking Congress! — is trying to step in and regulate college athletics?

How did we get to the point that federal, state and district courts, not coaches, schools, conferences or the NCAA, are deciding who can and can't play college football?

How did we get to the point that coaches are shamelessly abandoning their teams in the middle of a playoff run, and schools are shamelessly rehiring coaches who were justifiably kicked to the curb?

How did we get to the point that schools and conferences are playing ruinously expensive, traumatic games of chicken with one another, to the point that conferences are now actively talking about booting out stubborn former national champions ?

How did we get to the point that so many rivalry games have been vaporized that it's big news when one like USC-Notre Dame is coming back, instead of that being a foundational, load-bearing game in the sport?

How did we get to the point that southwest legends Texas and Oklahoma are in the SEC, West Coast-based Stanford and Cal in the ACC, and extremely non-Midwestern schools from California, Washington and Oregon are in the Big Ten?

How did we get to the point that players are getting paid for their services, when we spent decades prosecuting them for the crimes of accepting free burgers? (This is not a complaint, actually; I'm more impressed that college sports finally figured out how to fairly compensate the guys who make this multibillion-dollar enterprise run.)

How did we get to the point where players can hop from school to school, heedless of either tradition or common sense, turning entire rosters into hordes of roaming freelancers and destroying any lasting connection with their university?

Seriously, how did we get to the point that the greatest sport in America — we will hear no counter-arguments — has devolved from joyful celebration of everything that makes sports great into vindictive, litigation-filled chaos? How many times can this sport keep fumbling the ball in the open field?

You could say this is all old-man-yells-at-cloud carping, but this has all happened within the past four years — and in some cases, the past four days . A 12-year-old could yell at the clouds over this.

In the same way that you can pinpoint the exact moment when a tight football game reaches its apex — inside two minutes, fourth down, trailing team deep in the leading team's territory — you can sense that we're at the hinge point for all of the courtroom- and congressionally incited madness of the past few years. And it all centers, of course, on a provocative little school down in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

Fascinating, maddening and never dull, LSU possesses the exact combination of institutional wealth, alumni devotion and mercenary shamelessness, at a precise moment of enticing regulatory and judicial loopholes, to allow this kind of only-in-2026 madness to flourish.

Briefly — or as briefly as we can make a saga that, honestly, is its own curriculum at this point — dozens of Class of 2022 players who were not grandfathered in by the NCAA's new "five in five" eligibility regulations have sued for their right to one more year of eligibility. The issue is that some of these players had already moved on to their post-college employer — the NFL — and now want back in on some lucrative NIL dollars.

The major conferences, and most member schools, have basically told the players to get on with their lives. Sometimes you miss out just by being born too early. (How much NIL money do you think, say, Cam Newton or Deion Sanders would have earned had they been able to, legally?)

But because any hour that's unbilled is a wasted hour, at least in the minds of certain attorneys, many of those players have tried to sue their way back into college. And because there's always a local judge who can find legal precedent to help good ol' State U., those players managed to win the right to rejoin college rosters. And because there are always opportunistic coaches who will look for any legal or quasi-legal edge to succeed, these players are going to be welcomed back onto rosters. Well, welcomed by the coaches, at least.

Right now, Lane Kiffin and LSU are doing this dance, apparently allowing a couple players to join the Tigers roster with a kind of mock-shrug — Hey, we didn't try to do this, but we're just following the court's orders . And the rest of the SEC is rightfully furious; Yahoo Sports' Ross Dellenger notes that 15 schools are opposed to the idea . (Keep in mind: the SEC has 16 member institutions.)

The issue here isn't really whether these particular players are added to this particular roster. (The players they might displace have a definite beef, but that's very much a locker room issue.) The point here is 1) a court is telling a league who is and isn't eligible and 2) THIS DEFIES COMMON SENSE!

As we saw with NIL, when outside institutions start taking a hard look at the way colleges do business, the entire superstructure is in real danger of collapse. The games would continue, the band would keep playing, but the idea that college football could devolve and dissolve into a collection of disconnected leagues, much like minor-league baseball, isn't as far-fetched as you might think.

You can trace all of the "How-did-we-get-to-the-point-wheres" to the tsunami of revenue rolling into the sport, money that effectively obliterates decades of tradition. Every time Money and Tradition collide, Money wins in a five-touchdown rout. And in the stands, plenty of fans, broadcasters and university officials who were once wearing Tradition jerseys have happily changed into Money ones now that they've seen how the game is going.

But nobody roots for Money. Nobody roots for new broadcast agreements, or for escalating coaching salaries, or congressional acts "protecting" college sports. People root for their teams on the field, the competition and tradition and aura that surrounds a college football Saturday. Every single grubby money-grab, every tacky justification, every courtroom filing only tarnishes the game a little more.

There will come a point when every college football fan will decide if they've had enough — if the sport has drifted too far from its golden days to enjoy any longer. That day came for boxing and horse racing. College football may now be too big to fail, but it's definitely not too big to avoid losing its soul.

articles.title: Texas High School Football: North Crowley’s shutout of Aledo was historic
articles.summary: North Crowley wasted no time reminding the rest of Texas that its once again a top contender in Class 6A-D1. The Panthers blanked Aledo 26-0 in a matchup of...
articles.body:
North Crowley wasted no time reminding the rest of Texas that its once again a top contender in Class 6A-D1. The Panthers blanked Aledo 26-0 in a matchup of top-10 teams in the Lone Star State — per the Rivals Composite Rankings — on Friday night.

The game was Aledo's first since moving up to the 6A classification. The rude welcome was unfortunately a historic one for the Bearcats. It's the first time that Aledo has been shutout since 2003, when it lost 17-0 to Denton Ryan .

To get a better idea as to how much of an offensive struggle the game was for the visitors, take this stat courtesy of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram's Charles Baggarly: Aledo finished with -17 rushing yards on 40 carries.

Aledo had just 178 yards of total offense. North Crowley scored all 26 of its points in the first half. Senior quarterback Jacob Torres threw three touchdowns, the first of which went to junior wide receiver Damarion Mays , a top-100 prospect in the 2028 cycle.

It's a sobering start to the year for Aledo, which still ranks as the No. 59 team in the nation and No. 10 team in Texas, according to the Rivals Composite Rankings. Up next for the Bearcats is their home-opener vs. Waco Midway this Friday, Sept. 4.

North Crowley continues string of high-profile games

The 1-0 start will have new head coach DeMarcus Harris excited about what the 2026 season could bring North Crowley, but there's no time to ponder the future. The first half of the Panthers' schedule is incredibly challenging.

Up next, the No. 36 team in the nation and No. 6 team in Texas hosts Southlake Carroll , the No. 5 team in the state. No. 13 Summer Creek will then come to town and a road trip to No. 3 Duncanville will follow. Every game will be loaded with prospects.

North Crowley's secondary is incredibly loaded itself. Senior four-star cornerback Jerry Outhouse , senior three-star safety Elijajuan Houston and junior three-star safety Brock Lacy lead the way. Outhouse, a UCLA commit, is the No. 16 CB in the 2027 cycle.

It's also worth noting that the Panthers almost brought in Five-Star Plus+ CB John Meredith , the former No. 2 overall prospect in the nation, but he was ruled ineligible and opted to reclassify and join the Texas Longhorns early instead.

Mays is the top receiver target for Torres, but there's also junior three-star WR Hayden Green , senior three-star tight end Jeramie Cooper and senior three-star running back G'yrell Smith , a North Texas commit.

Su llegada confirma nuestro deseo de contar con un defensa experimentado, acostumbrado a las exigencias del más alto nivel", ha subrayado Jean-Louis Leca, director deportivo del Lens. "Ha vivido esta competición con la selección francesa, el FC Barcelona y, durante las dos últimas temporadas, en la Premier League. Sus cualidades están más que demostradas en la Ligue 1. Su capacidad para ganar duelos, su lectura del juego y su excelente técnica de pase nos impresionaron. Su carácter jovial será un gran activo para el vestuario. El interés fue mutuo y Jean-Clair estaba muy ilusionado por unirse a nosotros", ha insistido Leca.

Tennessee announced the passing of former football assistant coach Kippy Brown . He was 71.

"We mourn the passing of Kippy Brown, one of the greatest wide receivers coaches in Tennessee history," Tennessee announced Tuesday . "Our deepest condolences go out to his family, friends and former players."

Brown served three stints as wide receivers coach for the Vols from 1983-89, 1993-94 and 2009. A Sweetwater, Tennessee native, he helped establish Wide Receiver U at Tennessee.

Brown served as Tennessee's interim head coach after the Vols parted ways with Phillip Fulmer in 2008.

He also coached in the NFL, winning Super Bowl XLVIII with Seattle . Brown also coached with the Jets, Tampa Bay, Miami, Green Bay, Houston and Detroit.

The former Tennessee assistant coach played at Memphis and was inducted into the Tennessee Sports Hall of Fame in 2019. Brown also coached at Memphis and Louisville in college.

Brown served as a head coach in the XFL with Memphis in 2001, compiling a 5-5 record.

articles.title: El Elche se lanza a por Lama
articles.standfirst: El Granada se mantiene firme y solo daría luz verde a la operación si la oferta se acerca a sus pretensiones
articles.summary: El Granada se mantiene firme y solo daría luz verde a la operación si la oferta se acerca a sus pretensiones
articles.body: En las últimas horas de mercado todo se agita y la necesidad aprieta, un escenario peligroso para el Granada, que cuenta con varios jugadores apetecibles en su plantilla. Este es el caso de Manu Lama, por el que han preguntado varios equipos de Primera en las últimas horas. El último en sumarse a la lista de interesados ha sido el Elche, obligado a buscar un recambio para Affengruber, cuya salida ha dejado dinero fresco en las arcas del conjunto ilicitano, que parece decidido a hacerse con los servicios del central rojiblanco. Lama, cuyo contrato con el Granada finaliza en junio de 2027, ya estaba en el radar de equipo como el Depor o el Alavés, aunque ninguno había llegado a poner sobre la mesa una oferta interesante para el conjunto andaluz. Los rojiblancos darían luz verde a la salida de uno de sus jugadores más importantes por unos 5 millones de euros, una cifra a la que ningún pretendiente se ha acercado por el momento, aunque el Elche estaría decidido a llegar a un acuerdo con el club antes del cierre del mercado. Por otro lado, el proceso de venta del Granada sigue su curso, pero mientras todo se formaliza el club ha decidido introducir cambios en su estructura de gobierno y dirección, en el “marco del proceso de fortalecimiento institucional y deportivo de la entidad”, dándole poderes a Beristain, que llevaba semanas semanas ejerciendo en la sombra. La entidad nazarí ha confirmado que Ignacio Beristain se incorpora al Consejo de Administración del Granada, ejerciendo con Sophia Yang la presidencia del club andaluz, un movimiento que en la práctica supone un traspaso de poderes a la espera de que el proceso de venta concluya. Paralelamente, Alfredo García Amado deja de formar parte del Consejo de Administración y cesa de sus funciones como Director General del Granada. Amado llegó al conjunto nazarí en 2022, cuatro años en los que la situación del club se ha deteriorado de forma preocupante. El Granada asegura que afronta esta nueva etapa con el “firme compromiso de mantener la estabilidad institucional, seguir fortaleciendo su proyecto deportivo y trabajar en la consecución de los objetivos establecidos en la temporada.

articles.title: El Málaga libera una ficha y cede a Arriaza al Estepona
articles.standfirst: El canterano renueva antes hasta 2028
articles.summary: El canterano renueva antes hasta 2028
articles.body: Pablo Arriaza seguirá vinculado al Málaga CF hasta 2028 y jugará esta temporada cedido en el Estepona. El canterano amplía su contrato con la entidad blanquiazul y afronta ahora un nuevo paso en su formación lejos de La Rosaleda. La operación responde a la hoja de ruta que el Málaga tenía marcada para el centrocampista. El club siempre ha considerado a Arriaza como un jugador de futuro y patrimonio de la entidad, pero entiende que necesita acumular minutos y experiencia competitiva antes de dar el salto definitivo al primer equipo. Se ha comparado su caso con el del ’22’ o el ’10’, dos estrellas del equipo a día de hoy. Arriaza, de 22 años, se ha convertido en uno de los productos destacados de La Academia. Formado en el CD Tiro Pichón, el mediocentro fue una pieza importante del Atlético Malagueño durante la pasada campaña, con 27 partidos disputados en Segunda Federación. Además, tuvo presencia habitual en los entrenamientos del primer equipo y llegó a debutar con el Málaga en Copa del Rey frente al Talavera. Su buen rendimiento le llevó incluso a realizar buena parte de la pretemporada a las órdenes de Juanfran Funes, que siempre ha defendido la importancia de encontrar el escenario adecuado para que el futbolista continúe creciendo. El técnico ya puso como ejemplo los caminos seguidos anteriormente por jugadores como David Larrubia o Dani Lorenzo para explicar la utilidad de una cesión. Ahora ese escenario será el Estepona y estará en Segunda RFEF. Arriaza se marcha al conjunto costasoleño para disfrutar de una continuidad que, en principio, sería más complicada de encontrar en un Málaga que acaba de regresar a Primera División.

articles.title: Enzo Fernandez transfer news: Manchester City agree £125m deal to sign Chelsea midfielder on Deadline Day
articles.summary: Enzo Fernandez joined Chelsea from Benfica for £107m in 2023; the Argentine played in Chelsea's first Premier League game of the season against Fulham but was not involved against Luton in the Carabao Cup and left out again when they faced Brighton
articles.body:
The deal matches the British record transfer fee Liverpool paid for Newcastle striker Alexander Isak during last year's summer Deadline Day .

Chelsea will make a £18m profit on the midfielder they signed for £107m three and a half years ago.

Fernandez made it clear he wanted a move to City where he will be reunited with his former Chelsea boss Enzo Maresca. The player will now take a medical and finalise his move to City.

Chelsea are working to bring in a replacement for the Argentina international. They have been pursuing Roma's Manu Kone and Monaco's Lamine Camara as well as exploring potential Premier League midfielders.

The transfer window shuts at 11pm but clubs can submit deal sheets to give themselves an extra two hours to complete deals beyond the deadline.

Carragher: Man City now Arsenal's closest challengers

"Myself and plenty of others have felt Chelsea will have a really good season. And I still believe that a lot of that is on the back of not having European football, having a new manager, the front three that they've got.

"But they're losing Enzo Fernandez, who, for me has been one of the big players for Chelsea.

"Manchester City look a lot stronger now. I would say they're going to be the biggest challenges to Arsenal right now.

"It is a really good squad. There's no doubt about that. There's been a lot of turnover. Losing Rodri was a big thing and I thought it would be really difficult to recover from that.

But if you said at the end of last season, they would bring in Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez, you'd say, that's a top midfield. They've paid top dollar for it, so it should be.

"That gives them the greatest chance of being the main challengers and maybe the only team who can really wrestle this title from Arsenal."

"Enzo Fernandez definitely wins. His agent wins because he's had two incredible moves.

"What Chelsea are trying to create is a culture and if a player doesn't want to be there, you've got to let them go.

"It feels that it might be the right thing to do. He wants to go work for his previous boss and you're going to get good money in. Some people will say to just keep him but if he doesn't want to be there, then it becomes very difficult.

"It leaves Chelsea a bit short in that area. Moises Caicedo looked like he picked up a knock the other day. Can you rely on Romeo Lavia? He is a top player but his injury record isn't great. Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer aren't those types of player.

"If they don't get a player in, it won't look such a clever move.

"If they get a Manu Kone in, it will certainly soften the blow. But he will be a loss because he is a very good player. But for £120m, it will help balance the books and may look like a smart move in time."
